title: BigQuery Architecture & Performance Optimization
exp: Google Cloud platform interviews center on BigQuery architecture (Dremel, Colossus, Capacitor), partitioning, clustering, and slot management.
pts: **BigQuery Storage & Compute Separation:** Dremel execution engine over Borg, Capacitor columnar storage over Colossus file system.
**Partitioning vs Clustering:** Date/Ingestion-time partitioning + multi-column clustering (up to 4 columns) for maximum query cost reduction.
**BigQuery Slots:** virtual CPUs for query execution; On-demand vs Reservations (Editions: Standard, Enterprise, Enterprise Plus).
**BigQuery BI Engine:** in-memory analysis service for ultra-fast sub-second dashboard rendering.
pr: Write DDL for a partitioned and clustered BigQuery table
Compare query bytes scanned before and after clustering

r: Deep mechanics of BigQuery Architecture & Performance Optimization under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.
Use profiling tools to measure actual baseline allocation before optimizing.
Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.
Favor simple, well-tested modular architectures over premature complexity.

qa.q: How do Partitioning and Clustering combine to reduce BigQuery query costs?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Partitioning splits tables into daily/monthly directories, allowing BigQuery to prune entire time blocks. Clustering sorts data within each partition by specific columns, allowing Capacitor storage to skip unreferenced file blocks within partitions.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: What is the difference between On-Demand and Reservations (Slots) pricing in BigQuery?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** On-demand charges per TB of data scanned ($6.25/TB). Slot reservations allocate dedicated query processing slots per hour (BigQuery Editions), providing predictable costs for enterprise workloads.
